questions.q: A SaaS company's customers complain that outages are detected late and fixed slowly. Leadership wants clear service-level objectives, end-to-end observability of its cloud workloads, a mature incident and problem management process, and patch and capacity management. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective addresses these capabilities?
questions.hint: Think about who keeps workloads running day to day at the agreed service levels, rather than who steers the overall cloud program.
questions.explanation: The Operations perspective covers observability, event, incident and problem management, change and release management, and performance and capacity management so services meet agreed levels. Governance focuses on program and project management, risk, cloud financial management and benefits tracking, not running and monitoring workloads.

questions.q: A developer's IAM user has an identity-based policy that allows s3:PutObject on all buckets. The bucket named 'payroll' has a bucket policy with a statement that explicitly denies s3:PutObject to that developer's user ARN, with no conditions. What happens when the developer uploads an object to 'payroll'?
options: The upload succeeds, because identity-based policies take priority over resource-based policies
The upload is denied, because an explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides any allow
The upload is denied only if the developer signed in without MFA
The upload succeeds, because bucket policies apply only to anonymous users
questions.hint: Check whether the deny statement has any condition attached. If it has none, does anything else about the sign-in matter?
questions.explanation: IAM evaluates all applicable policies together, and an explicit deny always wins over an allow, whether it sits in an identity-based or resource-based policy. MFA only matters if a policy contains an MFA condition (such as aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent); this deny has no conditions, so it applies regardless of how the user signed in.

questions.q: A company's policy says every Amazon S3 bucket must have versioning enabled. It needs each bucket evaluated whenever its configuration changes, a recorded history of the bucket's settings over time for auditors, and noncompliant buckets fixed automatically through an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Which service meets these requirements?
options: AWS Config with a managed rule and automatic remediation
questions.hint: You need a service that records resource configuration over time and evaluates it against rules you choose.
questions.explanation: AWS Config records configuration history for resources, evaluates changes against Config rules, and can trigger Systems Manager Automation documents to remediate noncompliant resources. Trusted Advisor runs a fixed set of best-practice checks and gives recommendations, but it does not keep per-resource configuration history or let you define compliance rules with automatic remediation.

questions.q: A company runs a content management system on a fleet of Linux Amazon EC2 instances spread across three Availability Zones. All instances must read and write the same set of files at the same time, and storage should grow and shrink automatically as files are added or removed. Which storage service should the company use?
questions.hint: Look for a shared file system that many instances in different Availability Zones can mount at once.
questions.explanation: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, elastic NFS file system that many Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones can mount concurrently. An EBS volume is block storage tied to a single Availability Zone and is normally attached to one instance at a time, with a fixed provisioned size.

questions.q: An online store's web tier receives sudden bursts of orders during promotions, and the order-processing servers sometimes cannot keep up, causing lost orders. The company wants to buffer orders so that each one is stored durably until a processing server pulls it and finishes the work. Which service should it place between the two tiers?
questions.hint: The consumers should pull work at their own pace, and messages should wait until they are processed.
questions.explanation: Amazon SQS is a managed message queue that durably stores messages until consumers poll, process and delete them, decoupling producers from slower consumers. Amazon SNS pushes notifications to subscribers right away (pub/sub) and does not hold a backlog of work for consumers to pull later.

questions.q: A startup wants to run its application code without provisioning, patching or managing any servers or clusters of virtual machines. Which TWO AWS services provide serverless compute? (Choose two.)
questions.hint: One runs functions in response to events; the other runs containers without you managing the underlying instances.
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda runs code as functions and AWS Fargate runs containers for Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS, and in both cases AWS manages the servers. Amazon Lightsail is simpler than EC2 but still gives you virtual private servers that you manage and patch yourself.

questions.q: A healthcare customer asks a company to prove that the AWS infrastructure hosting its application has been independently audited, and requests a copy of AWS's SOC 2 report and PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance. Where can the company download these documents on demand?
questions.hint: You need AWS's own third-party audit reports, not a tool that assesses your own resources.
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for on-demand access to AWS's compliance reports, such as SOC and PCI reports, and for reviewing and accepting certain agreements. AWS Audit Manager helps you collect evidence about your own AWS usage for your audits; it does not provide AWS's third-party audit reports.

questions.q: A German bank is planning its first workload on AWS. Regulations require that customer data stays within the European Union. Which factor should be the PRIMARY consideration when the bank chooses an AWS Region?
options: The Region with the largest number of Availability Zones
The Region with the lowest prices for Amazon EC2
The Region where new AWS services launch first
questions.hint: Some selection factors are optional trade-offs; one of them is a legal requirement that rules out Regions entirely.
questions.explanation: Legal and regulatory requirements such as data residency come first when selecting a Region, because data stored in a Region stays there unless the customer moves it. Price, service availability and latency are important trade-offs, but only among Regions that already meet compliance requirements.

questions.q: Before migrating, a company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned architecture with Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS and Amazon S3, and share the estimate with its finance team. It has no AWS usage yet. Which tool should it use?
questions.hint: The workload does not exist on AWS yet, so there is no historical usage to analyze.
questions.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator lets you model planned services and configurations, see an estimated cost, and share the estimate with a link. AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts based on your actual past usage, so it cannot help before any usage exists.

questions.q: A research lab runs thousands of independent simulation jobs each week. Jobs checkpoint their progress, can be stopped and restarted at any time, and have no fixed deadline. The lab wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which Amazon EC2 purchasing option is MOST cost-effective?
questions.hint: The workload tolerates interruptions, so you can use spare capacity that AWS may reclaim.
questions.explanation: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at discounts of up to 90% compared with On-Demand, and are ideal for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads that can handle interruptions. Standard Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment for steady usage and offer smaller discounts than Spot for this kind of interruptible batch work.
